Level classification is inferred from identifiers; Single entries have not been assigned to challenge versus standalone menu categories.
Story titles are sourced, but story-to-level mappings have not been established.
Leader effects are descriptive; magnitude, stacking and applicability require gameplay verification.
Challenge rotation, current availability and live schedules were not checked.
Duplicate source entries are preserved; later localized names used for display may differ between tables.

source_entries.english: Makes [select value="{count}" 1="1 villager" 2="{count} villagers"] appear by the [FastMode.Props.Banner.Name].
Villagers walk faster for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"].
Plants and trees grow faster for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"].

Gives a {Concern.Nutrition.WithIcon} bonus for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"], reducing how much food villagers need. Satisfying this need activates the {UI.Boost.Nutrition.WithIcon}, increasing the villagers' movement speed while carrying resources.
Gives a {Concern.Community.WithIcon} bonus for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"]. Satisfying this need activates the {UI.Boost.Community.WithIcon}, increasing the reproduction rate.

Gives a {Concern.Entertainment.WithIcon} bonus for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"]. Satisfying this need activates the {UI.Boost.Entertainment.WithIcon}, increasing the villagers' movement speed.

Gives a {Concern.Heat.WithIcon} bonus for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"], shielding villagers from the cold. Satisfying this need activates the {UI.Boost.Heat.WithIcon}, making it easier to satisfy every other need.
Gives a {Concern.Wellness.WithIcon} bonus for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"]. Satisfying this need activates the {UI.Boost.Wellness.WithIcon}, increasing the villagers' lifespan.

Gives a {Concern.Refreshment.WithIcon} bonus for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"], keeping villagers cool in the heat. Satisfying this need activates the {UI.Boost.Refreshment.WithIcon}, making it easier to satisfy every other need.

Gives a {Concern.Hydration.WithIcon} bonus for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"], reducing how much water villagers need. Satisfying this need activates the {UI.Boost.Hydration.WithIcon}, making it easier to satisfy every other need.
Children grow up faster for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"].

Greatly increases birth rate for [select value="{count}" 1="1 day" 2="{count} days"]. Reproduction requires free {Concern.Housing.WithIcon}, so make sure to build enough houses for this bonus to be effective.

Hi! Welcome to the WorldWide All Stars Outlander Tournament™!
I’m Piper, a.k.a. Pen-and-Piper, and I’ll be in charge of your onboarding today.
I noticed you turned off the hints for the Campaign Tutorial, but since this is a whole new game mode, I switched them on!
You can totally turn them back off if you want, no biggie. I'll be just around the corner if you need me.
That's no problem at all, I'm committee-trained to show you the Outlanders™ experience.
Being an outlander is all about managing Resources and building the right Buildings.
(Also, Villagers are sort of a resource too, but you didn't hear that from me.)
So basically you need Villagers to work in Buildings so they can get Resources.
Wait, before you build anything: a quick lesson on moving the Camera around!
See? You're a natural. Now let's put that town to work!
Each day you'll draw three tiles and play one.
Today you can spawn some {Resource.Fruit.WithIconPlural}, place a {Building.Forager.WithIcon} or spawn a new Villager.
This is a drop of 6 {Resource.Fruit.WithIconPlural}, but we don't want this now.
This spawns a new Villager, but we don't want this now.
This allows you to build a {Building.Forager.WithIcon}. We'll get to this in a minute.
You could just spawn some {Resource.Fruit.WithIconPlural} now, but you wouldn't learn.
So just go ahead and select a {Building.Forager.WithIcon}.
Place the {Building.Forager.WithIcon} in the grid near those {Sources.FruitTree.WithIconPlural} over there.
C'mon, don't be a stinker and follow my lead please for now.
It's important that you learn this stuff.
Rotate it how you want it and hit Build to confirm.
Neat-o! See how the Building Panel opened up?
Villagers assigned to the {Building.Forager.WithIcon} will gather {Resource.Fruit.WithIconPlural} from nearby {Sources.FruitTree.WithIconPlural}.
Try assigning another Villager so they gather {Resource.Fruit.WithIconPlural} twice as fast!
Nice. You can close this panel now.
Hit the Play button to move to the next day.
Press {MenuButton} to enter menu navigation and hit the Play button to move to the next day.
Yikes on bikes! Your Villagers slept on the floor, did you see that?
That's no good, let's fix that rn!
Let's get some {Resource.Wood.WithIcon} to build a {Building.House.WithIcon}.
Luckily you drew a {Building.Lumberjack.WithIcon}, which lets your Villagers gather {Resource.Wood.WithIconPlural}! Phew…
Nice on ice! Did you remember to assign workers?
If you don't have enough Villagers you can always remove someone from another building.
Always check your worker assignments before starting the day, it's how the pros do it!
Hit Play when you're ready to go!
Mmmhh… you didn't draw a {Building.House.WithIcon} this time, bummer.
You see, tiles come from the Bag.
Open it up and you'll see.
Heck yeah! Look at all those possibilities.
Tiles are drawn semi-randomly from this Bag each day.
After you pick one, they return to the Bag and can be drawn again later.
In fact, let me show you something really cool…
Just close the Bag, you'll see…
If you don't like any of the tiles you drew, you can Skip!
This awards you with a special .
You can use them to buy tiles straight from the Bag, ain't that neat?
In fact, let's try it right now, go ahead and hit the Skip button.
Skipping was your action for the day, so now just hit Play to continue.
Don't worry, it's a good thing cause I get to teach you something. Just open the Bag.
Now that you have 1 you can buy any of these! They all cost the same.
But hold your horseradishes, once you buy one, the price goes up.
Next time you wanna buy something it will cost 2 .
Placing a {Building.House.WithIcon} near a building will make Villagers working there get to work faster!
For now, just go ahead and buy the {Building.House.WithIcon} you need.
Nice and neat! Now Villagers have a place to sleep (and make other villagers hehe...).
Buying from the Bag was your action for the day.
After that, you can't skip or pick from the tiles you drew.
Okie-dokie, we're ready to keep going!
Did you know following instructions is RAD?
It allows you to learn so you can be a PRO later.
Follow the instructions please, thank you SO much!
I think you're just about ready to complete your first Tournament level!
You complete levels when you complete the Objectives.
There's tons of information on the Top Bar™.
There's information about {Stat.Population.WithIcon}, {Concern.Housing.WithIcon}, Workers and much more!
For now let's focus on the Objectives.
Tap the Objectives icon in the bar.
This shows your progress in the level's Objectives.
This level only has one Objective. Click the arrow to learn more.
Looks like this level's Objective is to build 2 {Building.House.WithIconPlural}.
You're halfway there! You've got this one in the bag™.
WOOHOO! Objectives complete! I'd say I'm surprised, but honestly? I never doubted you for a second.
Tap the Success notification to make it official and finish your first tournament level!
You're a seasoned player! This’ll be easy peasy then.
The rules of the tournament are simple:
In Tournament Mode you play day by day, and you can only take one action per day.
Wanna see something cool? Go ahead and select the {Building.Forager.WithIcon} tile.
In Tournament Mode you don’t have to worry about building. That's so yesterday!
Though you still need to have the Resources necessary to build them... Ugh!
Don’t forget to assign workers at this stage or you won’t be able to until the next day!
Once you’ve taken your action, hit Play to see how the day plays out.
That was a good first day in my book!
Now you have a fresh set of action tiles for the day.
Let's build the {Building.Lumberjack.WithIcon} today so we can get some {Resource.Wood.WithIconPlural}!
Nice on ice! Did you remember to assign workers?
Another day, another set of tiles!
But where do they come from?!
Sweet on wheat! Let's spend that moneeeeeyyy.
Open the Bag to check out the goodies!
For now, just go ahead and buy a {Building.House.WithIcon}, just as an example.
Phew… we've come a long way, you're almost ready to complete the level on your own.
As you can see, Tournament Levels have Objectives too.
Complete the Objectives and you complete the level yada yada yada, you know the drill.
Oh wait hold the phone! I almost forgot about this.
There's tiles that provide Bonuses for needs (among other things).
That Community Bonus will satisfy the {Concern.Community.WithIcon} Need for a few days.
Unfortunately, I can't grant you any more complimentary <sprite name=Token> or I'll get in trouble.
You can wait until you draw one, or skip ahead until you've got enough <sprite name=Token> to buy one.
Hey good job on that last level!
It looks like we're doing some cooking this time, 36 bowls of {Resource.Stew.WithIconPlural} in fact. Holy Moly!
A pro like you doesn't need the full tour. If anything new pops up, you’ll hear from me!
To cook all those {Resource.Stew.WithIconPlural} we are gonna need a lot of {Resource.Veggie.WithIconPlural}!.
But {Resource.Veggie.WithIconPlural} don't just grow on trees, you know. We're going to need a {Building.Farm.WithIcon}!
Hmm, but we can't build it just yet. Select the {Building.Farm.WithIcon} to see what's missing.
Ah, there it is, we'll need {Resource.Stick.WithIconPlural} and {Resource.Clay.WithIcon} to build it.
Lucky for you, {Resource.Stick.WithIconPlural} are a natural resource found near trees, and Villagers will pick them up on their own.
But it looks like we're short on {Resource.Clay.WithIcon}. To make some, we'll need a {Building.ClayMaker.WithIcon}.
Just place the {Building.ClayMaker.WithIcon} anywhere you want.
Great! In a few days we'll have all the {Resource.Clay.WithIcon} we need for the {Building.Farm.WithIcon}.
{Resource.Clay.WithIcon} takes some time to make. Luckily, we just drew a bundle of 6 {Resource.Clay.WithIconPlural}.
Let's get that {Resource.Clay.WithIcon}! One step closer to our {Building.Farm.WithIcon}.
Heads up, this is a Single Use tile! Once you play it, it's gone for good. No hopping back into the Bag.
Ta-da! Your 6 {Resource.Clay.WithIconPlural} just plopped down right next to the [FastMode.Props.Banner.Name].
In the meantime, let's check out the Optional Objectives
Tap the Optional Objectives icon in the top bar.
This level only has Optional Objective. Click the arrow to learn more.
The Optional Objective requires building some {Building.PlankHouse.WithIconPlural}.
Now, {Building.PlankHouse.WithIconPlural} are made of… you guessed it: {Resource.Plank.WithIconPlural}.
And {Resource.Plank.WithIconPlural}? Those are just {Resource.Wood.WithIconPlural} that've been run through a {Building.Sawmill.WithIcon}.
That's the whole chain. I'm sure you can take it from here. No hand-holding on this one!
Psst… a {Building.Sawmill.WithIcon} could come in handy for those {Building.PlankHouse.WithIconPlural} if you're chasing the Optional Objective. Up to you.
Pro tip: drop it near a {Building.Lumberjack.WithIcon} so workers don't have to lug {Resource.Wood.WithIconPlural} halfway across the map. Now that's efficient!
Some tiles add new tiles to the Bag. This {Building.Lumberjack.WithIcon} sneaks in a {Building.Sawmill.WithIcon}!
Now that the {Building.Sawmill.WithIcon} is in the Bag, it might show up in a future draw. Fingers crossed!
There's the {Building.Farm.WithIcon} we've been looking for.
A {Building.Farm.WithIcon} is no good if it doesn't have any fields. Thank goodness fields don't need any Resources!
Planting the {Field.Cabbage.WithIconPlural} will yield the {Resource.Veggie.WithIconPlural} we need.
Farmers will only work on the highlighted area around the {Building.Farm.WithIcon}, so try to cover as much of it as you can
You may have been wondering how to get those sweet {Resource.Stew.WithIconPlural}! Prepared food is made in the {Building.OpenKitchen.WithIconPlural}.
It takes raw ingredients and cooks them up in delicious award-winning {Resource.Stew.WithIconPlural}!
Baby, you're cookin' up a win!
As you know, {Building.Farm.WithIconPlural} need fields built around them to work.
But get this, the {Building.Farm.WithIcon} tile is Nested™.
What it means is after you place it, you immediately choose a follow-up tile.
Gee, look at you! You're all set to be the next Tournament Champion!
I just need to go over a few more details before I can complete your form.
No need for hand-holding this time. Show me what you've got!
Bet you're wondering what {Concern.Community.WithIcon} is! See, Villagers have needs.
{Concern.Housing.WithIcon} and {Concern.Nutrition.WithIcon} are basic needs, by now you know all about them two.
There are buildings made to satisfy those needs, and they also provide helpful Boosts.
You'll see them show up as you go along.
Each and every need feeds into your town's {Stat.Happiness.WithIcon}.
Tap the {Stat.Happiness.WithIcon} to see where each need stands.
Open up {Concern.Community.WithIcon} to see what it's all about.
Here are the basics about {Concern.Community.WithIcon}. You can open the Field Guide to dig deeper.
To bump up that {Concern.Community.WithIcon}, we'll be cooking up some {Resource.Stew.WithIconPlural} again. Yum!
Good news! We've already got two {Building.ChickenCoop.WithIconPlural} cranking out {Resource.Egg.WithIconPlural}.
All we need now is an {Building.OpenKitchen.WithIcon} to whip those {Resource.Egg.WithIconPlural} into delicious {Resource.Stew.WithIconPlural}!
Luckily you know all about it now, right? Right!
Uh-oh, we've got a teensy little problem here…
The {Building.ChickenCoop.WithIconPlural} and the {Building.OpenKitchen.WithIcon} are waaaay too far apart.
Your Villagers are taking ages hauling those {Resource.Egg.WithIconPlural} over to the {Building.OpenKitchen.WithIcon}!
Fun fact: Buildings like {Building.Market.WithIconPlural} or {Building.Warehouse.WithIconPlural} let you accumulate different Resources in one spot.
Time to figure out how to build a {Building.Market.WithIcon} so we can get those {Resource.Stew.WithIconPlural} cooking!
Just what we needed to round up all those {Resource.Egg.WithIconPlural}!
Knowing how to place these logistic buildings is the mark of a true Outlander Strategist.
The {Building.Market.WithIcon} can stash {Resource.Fruit.WithIconPlural}, {Resource.Veggie.WithIconPlural}, {Resource.Meat.WithIconPlural} and {Resource.Egg.WithIconPlural} all in one spot!
Hop into the Resources tab to pick and choose which resources get stored here.
Press {SwitchTabButton} to switch to the Resources tab, then pick and choose which resources get stored here.
Just pause the {Resource.Fruit.WithIconPlural} and your workers will focus on hauling {Resource.Egg.WithIconPlural} over here. Easy peasy!
Closed it? Tap the {Building.Market.WithIcon} to open it back up.
Hi! I just saw you built your first {Building.TradingPost.WithIcon}.
The {Building.TradingPost.WithIcon} lets you collect Resources native to this biome and trade them for those from another biome.
Open the Resources tab to choose the resource you want to receive.
Check that the right Resource is active.
Select the {Building.TradingPost.WithIcon} to check the active trade.

Bakery.discrepancy: Fuel discrepancy: the decoded balance is 5 Flour + 4 Sticks → 40 Bread. The field guide implies 5 Sticks for that output. Actual fuel use across complete cycles remains unverified.

claims: Field guide: Potato Field + Beet Field + Cabbage Field → 1 Veggie.
Construction: 6 Glass Pane + 6 Stone. Worker slots: 3.
Greenhouse field guide: enables farmers to plant fields and harvest vegetables in the Winterland biome.
Construction: 6 Glass Panes + 6 Stone. Worker slots: 3.
Field guide: 2 of any of Veggie, Meat, Egg + 1 Stick → 3 Stew.
Field guide: any 2 of Veggie, Meat or Egg (one shared count) + 1 Stick → 3 Stew.
Provides: each Stew shows Food 1 and Community 2.
Cost shows Clay and Stick; the amounts and the worker count were below the visible part of the screenshot.
earlier.discrepancy: The decoded steps burn 1 Stick into 5 fires and use one fire per cook, so the worked-out ratio is 1/5 Stick per 3 Stew; the field guide counts the whole Stick. Stew's own stored values restore Food 1 and no Community: the Community 2 the guide shows is its display value (ResourceBehaviour.Visual), and the Community a villager gets comes from eating at the Open Kitchen's social spots (4 units a visit).

Open Kitchen.discrepancy: The decoded steps burn 1 Stick into 5 fires and use one fire per cook, so the worked-out ratio is 1/5 Stick per 3 Stew; the field guide counts the whole Stick. Stew's own stored values restore Food 1 and no Community: the Community 2 the guide shows is its display value (ResourceBehaviour.Visual), and the Community a villager gets comes from eating at the Open Kitchen's social spots (4 units a visit).

Bottle Factory.discrepancy: The field guide shows 2 Sticks per Bottle; the decoded steps work out to 1 Stick per Bottle. Which one a cycle actually burns is untested.

Cheesery.discrepancy: The field guide lists only 1 Stick under Needs: the Cheesery milks its own cows, so Milk never appears as an input. The decoded steps burn half a Stick per wheel of 6 Cheese.

Fishing Dock.discrepancy: The field guide shows the catch as a range, 0 to 2 Meat, which matches the stored random catch per spot.
